document.title: U.S. Embassy Kabul Cable 003681, "Confronting Afghanistan's Corruption Crisis"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Confidential] Neumann calls corruption a major threat and lists its causes. He acknowledges working with unsavory political figures; the full 2014 release names Karzai's half-brother (CIA-paid) and provincial governors on covert payrolls. It also flags narcotics and opium as a threat to the state.

events.description: Ambassador Neumann sends cable on corruption crisis and recommends Karzai remove corrupt officials.
Afghan parliamentary elections, marking the end of the Bonn Process; Karzai promised to clean house afterward.
USAID conducted a comprehensive Afghan corruption assessment.

key_claims: Afghan corruption has grown from customary practice into a major threat to the state since 2001.
Contacts fear the narcotics sector could push corruption out of control.
The cable says Karzai must remove corrupt officials including Ahmad Wali Karzai, Jan Muhammad and Gul Agha Shirzai.
Coalition ties with corrupt local commanders, such as contracts at Kandahar Air Field, are said to perpetuate corruption.
Ahmad Wali Karzai is widely accused of narcotics trafficking and is seen as immune from action.
